name: Service Events
os_min: Event ID 7045 requires Windows Server 2008 R2+; 4697 auditing requires Windows 10+
location: System.evtx (Win7+): Event IDs 7034/7035/7036/7040/7045; Security.evtx (Win10+, requires auditing enabled). Event ID 4697
purpose: Analyzes logs for suspicious Windows service creation, persistence, and services started or stopped around the time of a suspected compromise; service events also record account information.
key_fields: Event ID 7034 (System log): service crashed unexpectedly
Event ID 7035 (System log): service sent a Start/Stop control
Event ID 7036 (System log): service started or stopped
Event ID 7040 (System log): start type changed (Boot | On Request | Disabled)
Event ID 7045 (System log, Win2008R2+): a service was installed on the system
Event ID 4697 (Security log, Win10+): a service was installed on the system, requires auditing enabled
normal_baseline: Service creation/start/stop events correspond to known software installs, Windows updates, and expected maintenance windows.
anomalies: Event ID 7045 for a service with a suspicious ImagePath, an unsigned binary, or a name mimicking a legitimate Windows service
A service repeatedly crashing (7034) coinciding with a known attack technique that targets that specific service or process
7040 start-type change flipping a security-relevant service to Disabled shortly before or during an incident
4697 present with no corresponding 7045, or vice versa, when both logs should be capturing the same install and auditing is enabled for both. Suggests log tampering or a gap in visibility
anti_forensic_notes: A large amount of malware and worms in the wild use services for persistence and privilege; services started on boot illustrate persistence (desirable to malware), and services can also be intentionally crashed via attacks like process injection to disable defensive tooling. 4697 requires the Audit Other Object Access Events subcategory to be enabled, which many environments don't turn on by default, leaving 7045 as the only reliable source.
interpretation: Treat System.evtx as the baseline source for service lifecycle events (available without extra auditing) and Security.evtx's 4697 as a bonus corroborating source only where that audit policy is already enabled. Cross-reference the service name/ImagePath against the `services-persistence` artifact's registry-level view (CurrentControlSet\Services) to confirm what the service was actually configured to run.
